branch.new_demand: Prove that the construction produces the perpendicular bisector.

questions.skill: Justify the perpendicular bisector construction
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: To construct the perpendicular bisector of AB, arcs of radius r (more than half of AB) centered at A and B meet at P and Q. Prove that line PQ is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
questions.prompt_markup: To construct the perpendicular bisector of AB, arcs of radius r (more than half of AB) centered at A and B meet at P and Q. Prove that line PQ is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
questions.correct_answer: PQ is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
questions.required_method: Use the converse of the perpendicular bisector theorem for P and for Q.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof. Essential: PA = PB = r and QA = QB = r; each of P and Q is on the perpendicular bisector (converse); two points determine that line. Alternative: SSS gives congruent triangles APQ and BPQ, then SAS/linear pair at the midpoint.
